checks: With unit Euclidean continuous normal, the nonnegative buffer and outward kernel change the old capture only within their respective slabs of widths at most εF√λ_+ and δ√λ_+. Each parallel section is bounded by the projection ball's (d−1)-volume, including one in dimension one. Summation over the fixed base and taking infima give the pointwise comparisons.

After Γ(u)=1, the stated inequalities preserve evaluations in the active band and retain strict full or empty saturation outside it. At the minimum-norm feasible tilt, a direction orthogonal to the active row span is feasible locally in both signs, so the tilt lies in that span. Independent rows have bounded right-hand sides and come from one finite list, giving a uniform tilt bound. The compact parameter minimum is continuous by joint dominated convergence and achieves a maximum on each fiber, with pure-base values constant there.

The largest fiber has volume at least 1/|P|. Its centroid gives raw depth at least γ_d/|P| through its own trace. At an own-boundary point, the finite dual affine support majorant produces a zero ordinary cap and the threshold shift to a nearby point costs at most the stated section bound times the point distance. Combining with the uniform smoothing bounds yields the own-ball radius.

For every Γ-unit normal both slab planes lie within r/2 of the mark, and all intermediate ball sections have area at least ω_(d−1)(√3r/2)^(d−1). Coarea gives 1/|u|≥√λ_−, and ψ integrates to one, so the bound is uniform including the ramp.

A large finite multiple of any pure-base normal preserves full/empty capture at nonzero base drifts. At zero drifts the original cap contains the full fibers; the own ball supplies positive strict loss below the full-capture plane. Thus pure-base caps cannot beat the compact nonvertical minimum. The original §6/§7 locators match these calculations.

dependencies.mapping: The complete P and positive Minkowski-compatible fibers satisfy the canonical hull profile theorem. Its f is nonnegative, continuous and concave with zero own-boundary values and sampled bound at most one. The general-profile variant only uses the stated uniform bound and continuity.

The finite positive convex fibers satisfy the support LP, whose dual provides an affine majorant of every sampled support height attaining the height at the own base. Extend it from the affine span of P.
Use its m=a full-volume case on the largest positive fiber. The full-volume centroid has each containing own cap of volume at least γ_d times that volume.

overlap.comparison: Contains the ramp comparison and clipping and proves positive coarea under its strict ordinary trial and compact sublevel assumptions, with a global body-minimum conclusion. The draft treats smooth outward kernels as well as the ramp and arbitrary bounded nonnegative concave profiles in a fixed controlled family without the trial or sublevel assumption.

readability: The positive slab bound holds in the stated Γ-unit normalization. The fixed-family statement does not rely on a variational compactness conclusion for a larger body class.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The fixed controlled family admits exact compact clipping and an attaining nonvertical cap at every sufficiently small-parameter deepest mark. The same own-ball estimate gives positive coarea for each attaining cap.
